newsitem.title: USA: Quad ministers said near deal on info-tech pact.
newsitem.headline: Quad ministers said near deal on info-tech pact.

text.p: U.S. and European Union trade chiefs are close to a deal on an information technology pact they say they would like to be launched at a high-level World Trade Organization meeting this year, trade sources said.

Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky and European Union Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan met early Saturday in an effort to work out a deal that would clear the way for a statement of support for the Information Technology Agreement (ITA) from the Quadrilateral (Quad) trade partners -- the United States, Japan, Canada and European Union-- meeting this week in Seattle, the sources said.
The trade sources said Barshefsky and Brittan were likely to strike a deal to settle the dispute that centered on a U.S.-Japan semiconductor arrangement renewed this July.

The European Union has expressed concern about the arrangement shutting European firms out of Japan's market, but U.S. trade officials have said Europe was welcome to join the arrangement as long as they were willing to commit to rapid elimination of import tariffs on computer chips.
The ITA would eliminate tariffs on a wide range of electronic equipment including computers, chips, software and telecommunications equipment by 2000.
Trade officials have said that Quad support for the ITA is crucial in order for the agreement to be launched at the December meeting of WTO trade ministers in Singapore.
